title: Elastic potential energy
examples: What is the relationship between the force and the extension of a spring?
How do I calculate the energy stored in a stretched spring?
Can you show me how the area under the force-extension graph relates to energy?

explain.say: Today we are learning about elastic potential energy stored in springs.

items: Energy is stored when a spring is stretched.
The formula for this energy is ½kx squared.
k is the spring constant and x is the extension.

explain.say: The spring constant, k, measures how stiff a spring is.
The extension, x, is the distance the spring stretches from rest.
The energy stored is calculated using the formula ½kx squared.
The area under the force-extension graph gives the stored energy.
When you stretch a spring, the work done on it equals the stored energy.

faq.q: Does the spring have to return to its original length?
faq.a: Yes, the energy stored is the maximum energy when it is fully stretched or compressed.
asks: What is the energy when the spring is released?
Does the spring need to go back to zero?

faq.q: What are the units for the spring constant k?
faq.a: The unit for the spring constant k is newtons per meter, or newtons per meter.
asks: What units do I use for k?
Is it newtons or newtons per meter?

faq.q: If I double the stretch, what happens to the energy?
faq.a: Because the energy uses x squared, doubling the stretch increases the energy by a factor of four.
asks: How does energy change if I stretch it more?
Is it linear or squared with the stretch?

faq.q: Can I use the area under the graph method always?
faq.a: Yes, the area under the force-extension graph always represents the work done, which is the stored potential energy.
asks: Is the graph method always correct?
Does the area always equal the energy?

faq.q: What is the difference between force and energy?
faq.a: Force is a push or a pull measured in newtons, while energy is the capacity to do work, measured in joules.
asks: Are force and energy the same thing?
What is the difference between the two measurements?

facts: Elastic potential energy is stored when an object stretches or compresses a spring.
The formula used to calculate this energy is E = ½kx squared.
The spring constant k is a measure of the stiffness of the spring.
Graphically, the work done equals the area under the force-extension graph.

quiz.say: A spring stretches 0.2 meters. If its spring constant is 50 newtons per meter, what is the stored energy?
quiz.why: You use the formula ½kx squared: one half times 50 times 0.2 squared equals one joule.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you calculate only x squared and forget to multiply by k.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you multiply k times x, forgetting the one half factor.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you use the wrong formula, perhaps thinking it is kx.

quiz.say: If the force-extension graph is a right triangle with a base of 1 meter and a height of 20 newtons, what is the stored energy?
quiz.why: The area of a triangle is one half times the base times the height, giving ten joules.

wrong.1: This mistake happens if you calculate the area as a full rectangle, ignoring the triangle shape.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you calculate the area as just the base length.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you square the force value instead of using the area formula.

quiz.say: A spring has a spring constant of 20 newtons per meter. If the stored energy is 5 Joule, what is the extension?
quiz.why: Rearranging the formula gives x equals the square root of two times the energy divided by k, which is zero point five meters.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you incorrectly use the value of k as the extension.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you calculate x by dividing the energy by k, forgetting the square root.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you calculate x by multiplying the energy by k.
